full_judgment: 10. It appears that there was a glaring suppression of fact by the writ petitions before the learned Judges of the High Court Division who were led to believe that after the initial order of requisition had been set aside in appeal by Mollah Co-Operative Housing Society Ltd. no fresh proceeding for requisition and acquisition of the lands in question was taken by the Government. This is belied by the order of the Joint Secretary, Ministry of Land Administration and Land Reforms (Annexure-C) which was very much before the High Court Division. On this aspect the statement of the Joint Secretary runs as follows; "On 22-10-64 again the orders of requisition under section 3 were made and on 21-9-64 proceedings u/s5(1) &5(3) appear to have been taken. " The Joint Secretary only doubted if the notices under sections 5(la) and 5(3) were actually served upon the parties concerned. It is quite likely that-the service return of these notices got missing during the transit of the concerned records to and from the Anti-corruption office where the same rested for a considerable time. This was noticed by the Joint Secretary in his order. Under section 114(e) of the Evidence Act one has to presume that the official acts have been regularly performed. Nothing was produced by the writ petitioners in rebuttal of the presumption. It also transpires from the said order of the Joint Secretary that Shah Sufi Emaduddin Ahmed Chisty made representations to the Government for derequisition of the lands. He also appeared before the Land Acquisition Officer and made his claim for compensation. And we have it from the order of the Ministry of Land Administration and Land Reforms (Annexure-D) that in Title Suit No.156 of 1966 .Shah Sufi Emaduddin Ahmed Chisty in his written statement admitted that he had received notices under section 5(1a) and 5(3) of the Act. There is no denying the fact that the said Shah Sufi Emaduddin Chisty was fully aware of the acquisition notices. Admittedly the Government went into possession of the disputed land as far back as in 1964 immediately after the initiation of the acquisition proceeding. Therefore there is no reason why Shah Sufi Emaduddin Chisty should not have been aware of the proceeding. The writ petitioners who are his transferees entered the scene only recently and therefore no question of fresh service of notice of acquisition on them arises.
